details:
TerraShift AI is a NASA-powered agricultural adaptation and crop-rotation decision-support platform designed to help smallholder and commercial farmers turn environmental data into practical multi-season planting strategies. Rather than acting as a passive weather dashboard, it evaluates how historical climate trends, current environmental stress, soil conditions, and farmer goals affect which crops should be planted next.

Core Architecture & Design Principles

  • Deterministic Engine Over LLM Guessing: All crop-rotation scores, rankings, and agronomic penalties are calculated by a rule-based Python engine (NumPy/Pandas) backed by a 36-crop indicative reference catalog (crop_knowledge.json). An optional language model (via Vultr Serverless Inference) translates the finished JSON output into plain-language explanations, and a strict validator rejects the AI text if it introduces any number not present in the computed results.
  • Strict Evidence Separation: Observed historical data (10-year daily meteorology from NASA POWER and visual imagery from NASA GIBS), short-term numerical forecasts (Meteomatics with a keyless Open-Meteo fallback), and research-backed agronomic guidance (Tavily filtered to authoritative institutions like FAO, ICAR, and CGIAR) are kept strictly separate and labeled.
  • Transparent Uncertainty & Missing-Data Handling: Missing farm inputs (such as unmeasured soil pH, organic carbon, or unconfigured Earthdata NDVI credentials) are explicitly flagged and penalize data-quality confidence scores rather than being invented or smoothed over. The system outputs relative suitability scores and indicative water/nitrogen budgets rather than fabricated yield predictions.
  • Vultr Infrastructure Backbone: Deployed on Vultr Cloud Compute using Docker, with PostgreSQL for persistent farm profiles and Vultr Serverless Inference for grounded report narration.
